newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends sharply higher on monsoon concerns.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends sharply higher on monsoon concerns.

text.p: CBOT rice futures posted double-digit gains on Friday, powered by concerns the monsoon in India may be ending early, traders said.
Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said in his international weather outlook that rains in India have started to diminish in the last few days.

"This is a very unusual situation to occur during the middle of August," Davis wrote. "It means one of two things. Either the monsoonal activity is taking a break and it will rebuild later on in August or the monsoon is starting to retreat.

"If it is retreating, it would be very detrimental since the crops still have a long ways to go before they reach maturity, partly because they were planted late," Davis wrote. "In other words, the crops need four to six more weeks of rain to develop normally."
Rice ended 17 to nine cents per cwt higher with September up 14 at $9.78. Volume was estimated by CBOT at 450 lots, above Thursday's actual volume of 382 lots.
Traders said LFG was a key buyer while locals were said to be active on both sides of the market.
